documents.title: DSA coding course - Java and Python
Browser rendering, Web Components and storage

sections.title: DOM, CSSOM and rendering
sections.reviewNote: A style change does not always trigger layout and paint; render-blocking CSS depends on context.

sections.title: Document objects and DOM methods
sections.reviewNote: Document is an object. Its selection methods return elements or collections, not methods.

sections.title: Shadow DOM and encapsulation
sections.reviewNote: Closed mode is not a security boundary. Inheritance and explicit styling APIs cross some style boundaries.

sections.title: Shadow trees in the page and DevTools
sections.reviewNote: Shadow DOM exists in the live page; DevTools visualizes it. Widget implementations and browser controls vary.

sections.title: Custom elements, templates and slots
sections.reviewNote: These APIs can be used separately. A template is inert markup; a slot projects light-DOM content.

sections.title: Browser storage choices
sections.reviewNote: Quotas and retention vary by browser policy. A new tab can initially copy its opener session storage.

sections.title: Who writes browser storage?
sections.reviewNote: Storage APIs require application operations; cookie transmission follows matching and privacy rules.

sections.title: Password managers and autofill
sections.reviewNote: A website cannot enumerate the password vault, but page code can read a password field value before submission.

sections.title: Storage APIs and helper functions
sections.reviewNote: The supplied IndexedDB wrapper branch is unfinished; use real transactions and completion/error handlers.
